Main._ready reads WorldState and swaps CurrentZone via `_swap_zone_node` if a saved zone differs (main.gd:41-58), then `_boot_zone(entry_id)` (64-101) builds a brand-new `EcsWorld` (manual_tick=true) with 6 systems hard-coded in `_make_world` (104-115): PlayerInput, EnemyAI, Movement, Combat, Health, ViewSync, always in that order. `EcsBoot.boot` (ecs_boot.gd:16) turns parked ActorViews into entities, painted `solid` tiles into grid blocks, and markers (ZoneExit, PlayerUnlock, Gate, PickupSpawnPoint) into per-cell dictionaries on `EcsGrid` (exit_by_cell, player_unlock_by_cell, gate_by_cell, item_by_cell: ecs_grid.gd:24-33,123). Entities are ints, stores are `store_by_component[key][id]`.

PER FRAME: `Main._process` (118-136) polls restart_room and KEY_F3/F11/B directly, calls `ecs.tick(delta)` unless `room_ending`, then `_handle_events(ecs.drain_events())` (153-192), a big `match` on event type that drives HUD text, PrototypeBoard overlay calls, CameraRig.start_shake, SfxManager.play, WorldState writes (6 direct `save_state()` calls: 292,393,422,487,496,567) and zone travel (`_travel_to` 382-399: fade, swap zone, rebuild whole world; WorldState carries health). Systems talk only through components, `world.pending_events` and `world.damage_events`; ONLY ViewSyncSystem touches nodes, using hard-coded child paths and AnimationTree params (view_sync_system.gd:36-130). Enemy AI = utility scoring (enemy_ai_system.gd) with one global attack token (`world.attack_token_owner`); telegraph locks cells, damage checks the hero's CURRENT cell, so stepping out dodges. Content is .tres: EnemyDefinition -> MovementConfig/DecisionConfig/AttackPattern/VisualDefinition/DifficultyProfile/EnemyWeapon; AttackProfile (player); RoomObjective; RuleBook/RuleEntry; WorldGraph (zone_id -> PackedScene only, no map metadata). Room scenes are RoomEncounter (zone_id, board_size, room_message, objective) with RoomArt and Entry/Exit Marker2Ds; 6 Stage-1 zones plus the old 72x40 kingdom live in resources/world/world_graph.tres, and H1's Exit_To_Act2Toybox still targets `kingdom`.

PERSISTENCE: `WorldState` autoload (world_state.gd) loads user://world_state.cfg in _ready (line 29-30): one global ConfigFile, SAVE_VERSION 2, a version mismatch silently reset()s. It holds current_zone_id, last_entry_id, player_health_carry (never saved), taken_pickup_ids, opened_gate_ids, unlocked_rule_ids, player_unlock_ids. Death = scene reload after 0.85 s (main.gd:285-302), respawn at the last zone entry, full health; R reloads instantly (119-120).

extension_points.where: scripts/story/ (StoryLine, StoryBeat, SpeakerStyle Resources; StoryDirector presentation node), resources/story/*.tres, scenes/ui/dialogue_box.tscn, locale/*.po
extension_points.how: RECOMMENDATION: ship a small Resource-based system now, text stored by KEY in the translation file. StoryLine{speaker_id, text_key, emote, mode BLOCKING|AMBIENT, hold_seconds}; StoryBeat{id, lines[], steps[], once, requires_flags, forbids_flags, sets_flags, freeze_simulation}. The owner rewrites story by editing plain-text locale/en.po and reordering beats in the Inspector. This matches AGENTS.md:175 ('dialogue' is explicitly a typed .tres) and needs no approval. Keep the seam narrow (`StoryDirector.play(beat_id)`) so a `.dialogue` backend can replace the data source later. HONEST COMPARISON. Dialogue Manager v4 (https://github.com/nathanhoad/godot_dialogue_manager, https://dialogue.nathanhoad.net/): MIT, README says Godot 4.6+ (project is 4.6.3, so compatible but locked to it), script-like `.dialogue` text with conditions/mutations, stateless (game owns state), headless (game draws the balloon), native translation support: best ergonomics for a writer. Costs: a dependency (CLAUDE.md requires owner approval first), a plugin import step for `.dialogue` files (same headless-needs-import pitfall as class_name), and mutations call GDScript so they must be routed through a thin state object that only sets StoryFlags/emits events. Dialogic 2 (https://github.com/dialogic-godot/dialogic, https://docs.dialogic.pro/): MIT, needs Godot 4.5+, README/docs label it Alpha ('workflows may break'), visual+text timelines, characters/portraits, styles, variables, CSV translation; it brings its own variables/saving/layout system that overlaps WorldState, SfxManager and the Theme, and is built for portrait visual novels, heavy for a 640x360 pixel UI. Not recommended. ASK THE OWNER whether to adopt Dialogue Manager as the authoring layer after the base ships.

extension_points.how: Map research to hooks, not code. (1) Self-Determination Theory: games engage via competence, autonomy, relatedness (https://selfdeterminationtheory.org/SDT/documents/2010_PrzybylskiRigbyRyan_ROGP.pdf): competence = fair telegraphs + clear mastery moments (boss tests a learned verb); autonomy = loops/shortcuts and choice of approach (gates already exist); relatedness = the child (frequency and timing of presence is a tunable curve). (2) Failure as story: make death advance the relationship, 'take the sting out of failure' (Hades, https://gdconf.com/news/dive-dialogue-hades-gdc-2021); death-count-keyed child lines. (3) Peak-end: invest in B1/H1 and the finale and ending (item 18). (4) Anticipation and feedback: telegraph readability first, juice scaled to event size, hit-stop only when it clarifies. (5) Contrast and silence: quiet opening (no music, room tone, wake animation), loneliness -> companionship arc per NAR.1's emotional-arc diagram. (6) No lecture: child lines emotional not instructional (NAR.3). Add a validate() on StoryBeat/ZoneInfo that fails when a zone has no beat or an unflagged ambient line exceeds the rate cap, so the emotional curve is testable.

must_follow_rules: Authority order when docs disagree: CLAUDE.md > docs/ecs-conversion-plan.md > everything else. docs/ARCHITECTURE.md, docs/coding-standards.md ('No ECS', GridWorld, EnemyActor), AGENTS.md ('Do not introduce a strict ECS framework', GridWorld, EncounterDirector) and the /new-enemy command are stale node-era text; do not follow them (CLAUDE.md:16-18 'Editor-first, ECS runtime').

State = pure-data class in scripts/ecs/ecs_components.gd plus a key const (ecs_components.gd:7-19); decisions = a system in scripts/ecs/systems/ ticked by the world; systems talk only via components, world.pending_events and world.damage_events, never by calling each other; ONLY ViewSyncSystem touches nodes (CLAUDE.md:19-33).

Presentation (HUD/board/camera/main.gd and every new director/UI) consumes drain_events() only. The bridge (main.gd) is the only place allowed to write simulation flags such as PlayerTag.control_enabled, and persistence flows one way: bridge seeds the world at boot, world emits events, bridge writes WorldState (pattern: pickups main.gd:480-487, gates 492-500).

Content is data. New enemy/boss/skill/beat/line/zone/intervention = .tres (or .po for prose) + a scene, never hard-coded in scripts; never duplicate a value in code and a .tres; shared .tres are immutable at runtime, duplicate(true) before mutating (CLAUDE.md, coding-standards.md:84-93,154-158).

Research order is mandatory: Godot built-in first, then a proven addon (ASK THE OWNER before adding any dependency: Dialogue Manager/Dialogic/GUT/etc.), then custom code with the reason stated in the commit message (CLAUDE.md:34-39).

New editor-draggable component = extend EntityComponent in scripts/ecs/components/ (Inspector data + one apply(); zero logic). Animation transitions live in the actor's AnimationTree; ViewSync only publishes conditions and calls travel() on event edges; keyframe SpriteRoot, never MotionRoot; the cell slide is procedural and never keyframed.

Audio has three layers with one owner each: motion sounds = audio tracks inside actor clips (AudioPlayer, bus SFX); mixing = default_bus_layout.tres; event sounds = SfxManager registry played ONLY from the main.gd bridge (or MusicManager/JuiceDirector via drained events); systems never play audio (CLAUDE.md:28-33, /new-sound).

Self-documenting names: dictionaries state direction (actor_by_cell), timers state semantics (state_time_left), no abbreviations; every non-obvious data structure gets a ## doc comment (key -> value). Before renaming any @export, grep .tscn/.tres for the serialized name and grep for get('name')/set('name') strings (CombatComponent.wooden_sword/pencil_thrust are serialized in objects/actors/player.tscn).
No _draw() for actor/pickup bodies (Sprite2D + AnimationPlayer); overlays (board telegraphs, debug, grid lines) may use _draw().

Folder ownership: scenes/ = entry scenes, rooms, ui only; objects/ = reusable prefabs (autoload service scenes go in objects/services/ or objects/audio/); resources/ = .tres; scripts/ = behavior; assets/ = raw art; tools/ = build scripts. New scripts need their .gd.uid sidecar committed (tests/*.gd.uid are tracked).

A new class_name needs ONE `--editor --quit` import pass before strict-typed headless scripts that reference it will parse. Order: write code -> import -> run tests. Translations should use .po (no import pass needed, verified).

TileMap tile_map_data is a binary blob: never hand-edit; use a tools/ paint script. Prefer NEW small format-3 .tscn files without uid headers (the proven style of hud.tscn, rule_book.tscn, sfx_manager.tscn) over hand-editing scenes/main.tscn or objects/actors/player.tscn, which the human edits in the editor.

Preserve the human's files: stage explicit paths; never `git add -A`; leave .mcp.json, reports/, research_notes/ alone. One logical change per commit, why-focused message, on a branch (current: game-base). Commit message ends with the attribution line from the session's system-reminder.

Keep the playable slice and ALL tests green after every change; update the tests that assert what you change in the same commit (ecs.systems.size()==6, MusicPlayer in main.tscn, English HUD literals, fullscreen mode==3).
Tests/runs must use HOME=/tmp/unbound-pawn-godot and never touch the real user://world_state.cfg or user://settings.cfg; use explicit test paths and delete them afterwards.

Art direction, story tone, play feel and ending emotion are human-owned (AGENTS.md:64-90): scaffold systems and clearly marked PLACEHOLDER content, hand off with the Open/Tune/Goal/Try/Tell me format, never finalize art. The owner's 2026-10-12 message authorises building the full base (it supersedes task_plan.md's 'no implementation until owner approves the batch'), but not final prose or art.

Update progress.md (what + why + verification), bump task_plan.md phase status, add durable facts to findings.md; to avoid merge fights with parallel agents write per-lane fragments and let one integrator merge them.
Child help gets its own input action; do not bind it to R (restart_room). Unknown/absent autoloads must be tolerated via get_node_or_null('/root/Name') so headless tests keep running.

Design rules to honour from the specs: no tutorial spam from the child (NAR.3), boss identity through behavior before dialogue (NAR.5), telegraph sounds/visuals outrank music and particles (au1, FX.2), colour is never the only threat cue (FX.6/UI.6), HUD never covers combat cells and hides unused systems (UI.1).
pitfalls_seen: AUDIO BUS BUG (verified by a headless probe in a throwaway /tmp project on Godot 4.6.3): default_bus_layout.tres:4 defines bus/0 as 'SFX' with no Master. Godot forces bus 0 to be Master, so at runtime the buses are [Master, Music, UI] and `AudioServer.get_bus_index(&'SFX')` = -1. Every player/enemy AudioPlayer and SfxManager with bus=&'SFX' (objects/actors/*.tscn:353-354, sfx_manager.gd) silently falls back to Master, so an SFX volume setting would do nothing. run_tests.gd:169-176 only asserts the layout loads. Fix: add a real Master as bus/0 and shift SFX/Music/UI to 1/2/3 (via the editor Audio panel), and add a test asserting get_bus_index(&'SFX') != -1. docs/where-we-are.md section 3 already suspected this ('not verified at runtime').

The session-start git snapshot is stale: the tree was committed to branch game-base during this run. Re-run `git status` before editing; the untracked human files are .mcp.json, reports/, research_notes/.

Fresh clones/worktrees are NOT self-contained: assets/sprites/generated/{chess,tiles,maps,rooms}/ are gitignored and rebuilt by four tools/ generators (README 'First run'); T1/T2 room backgrounds reference generated/rooms/*.png. A parallel agent in a separate worktree or clone will fail zone-loading tests until it runs the generators + an import pass, or the orchestrator copies those folders. export_presets.cfg and build/ are also gitignored (only on this machine), and *.translation is ignored (another reason to use .po).

Pause does not exist and the Rule Book does not freeze the game: main.gd:574-581 only disables player control while enemies keep ticking (ecs.tick runs whenever !room_ending, line 132). No process_mode or tree pause is used anywhere in the repo.

B, F3 and F11 are polled with raw KEY_* in Main._process (main.gd:121-130) with manual edge-detect booleans: not remappable, not controller-capable, and they would stop working under tree pause. hud.tscn's HelpLabel hard-codes 'MOVE WASD ... RESET R DEBUG F3' (ships debug key to players).

R (restart_room) reloads the scene instantly with no confirmation (main.gd:119-120); death also hard-reloads (302), replaying the hero's `wake` animation and restarting the MusicPlayer that lives in main.tscn:26 (autoplay).

Zero localization: no tr()/TranslationServer anywhere; ~9 status literals in main.gd (169,202,214,216,223,343,403,499,568) with format strings, hud.gd labels (COURAGE/CELL/ENEMIES/'FIND SWORD'/'Q THRUST'), scene text, and Resource text. hud.set_courage hard-codes 3 pips: `'◇'.repeat(3 - value)` (hud.gd:39) even though HealthComponent allows 1-9.
hud.set_status is a single label with last-writer-wins semantics; _unlock_met_rules, damage, pickups and room messages all overwrite each other, so any story line routed through it will be clobbered.

WorldState: single global ConfigFile, loaded implicitly in _ready (the game silently resumes mid-world on every launch; testers can only start over by deleting user://world_state.cfg), save errors unchecked (world_state.gd:59), version mismatch silently wipes progress (66-68), 6 scattered save call sites in main.gd. HARNESS TO KEEP: bare `extends SceneTree` scripts in tests/, each with `_expect(cond, label)`, final `print('X TEST: PASS|FAIL')` and `quit(0|1)`; labels are English statements of a guarantee (they double as the spec). Run from project root with `G="../Godot.app/Contents/MacOS/Godot"; HOME=/tmp/unbound-pawn-godot "$G" --headless --path . -s tests/<name>.gd`. ORDER: write code -> `--editor --quit` import (new class_names, scenes) -> run_tests.gd -> each runtime test (ecs_runtime, ecs_combat, ecs_enemy, room_encounter_runtime, encounter_hud_runtime, zone_travel_runtime) -> import again must print no ERROR/Parse -> `git diff --check`. Add `tests/run_all.sh` (new file) that does exactly this and exits non-zero on any failure, and fix /verify to include zone_travel_runtime_test; every lane runs it before committing. Fresh worktrees need the four generators + import first (README 'First run').

PER NEW SYSTEM (copy the ecs_* style: build an EcsWorld with manual_tick=true, add only the system under test, create entities with add_component or EcsActorFactory, write intents/markers directly, call world.tick(0.016) in loops, assert on components and on world.drain_events()): ecs_trigger_test (enter fires once, once-flag, requires/forbids flags, ROOM_CLEAR, flag_set emitted, no fire for enemies); ecs_boss_phase_test (health ratio crossing swaps decision/attack/movement, transition invulnerability, boss_phase_changed payload, defeat emits boss_defeated, defeated boss skipped on re-boot via skipped_enemy_ids); ecs_skills_test (cooldowns per skill, unlock gating, Rule Step i-frames, guard negates damage); ecs_child_help_test (believe spend/recharge, cell_effect expiry, refusal on occupied cell, disrupted_left blocks); ecs_knockback_heal_test (cell push uses damage direction, heal clamps at max); rook/queen ray tests (rays stop at blocked_cells and occupied cells, row/column telegraph cells). Systems are exercised without any Node tree except ViewSync.

DATA VALIDATION (pattern at run_tests.gd:263-273 and RuleBook/EnemyDefinition.validate()): loop DirAccess.get_files_at over resources/story, bosses, skills, interventions, zones and call validate(); assert every StoryBeat/Prompt/Zone name key exists in locale/en.po and in each shipped locale (no dangling keys, no unused keys); every ZoneExit targets a zone in WorldGraph and a real entry (already done, extend); every zone has an entry and music theme; every boss has >=1 phase and a defeat beat; ambient-line rate cap; actor/room scenes keep the art-swap contract node paths and clip names (item 21).

PRESENTATION/FLOW TESTS (pattern: encounter_hud_runtime_test.gd): instantiate scenes, `await process_frame`, drive `_process(0.016)` by hand, set TranslationServer.set_locale('en'); title: New Game resets WorldState and clears the slot, Continue loads it, slot cards read meta only; pause: `get_tree().paused` freezes ecs tick (position unchanged after N process calls) and unpauses cleanly; StoryBox: typewriter reaches visible_ratio 1, BLOCKING sets ecs.frozen and restores control afterwards (including one-frame input guard), skip_all restores camera/HUD/time_scale; MusicManager: crossfade ends with one player at 0 dB and one silent, survives scene reload; JuiceDirector: Engine.time_scale returns to 1.0 after hit-stop and after a scene reload. End-to-end: boot final boss zone with the boss at 1 HP, damage it via world.damage_events, assert boss_defeated -> GameFlow ENDING -> credits -> title, and `completed` persists. A walk-through smoke test boots every zone in world_graph.tres in order T1..H1 (+ new zones), teleports the player to each exit cell and asserts the next zone boots (closes the 'nobody has walked T1->H1' gap).

summary:
Short answer to the owner: yes, a complete start-to-finish base is achievable, because the ECS core already has the right seams (marker -> EcsGrid dictionary -> system event -> bridge, content in .tres, drain_events for presentation). Roughly 22 systems are missing, none requires an addon, and the story can live in plain-text locale/en.po plus StoryBeat .tres files the owner rewrites. What cannot be made 'perfect' by agents: final art, prose tone, play feel and the ending's emotion are human-owned (AGENTS.md); the base should ship every beat as clearly marked placeholder and be designed so hand-drawn art and rewritten text drop in without code (art-swap contract, theme resource, keys in .po).

Key findings: (1) VERIFIED BUG: the SFX audio bus does not exist at runtime (default_bus_layout.tres bus 0 is forced to Master; get_bus_index('SFX') = -1), so any SFX-volume setting would silently do nothing: fix first. (2) .po translations load headlessly with no import pass (verified), which avoids the gitignored *.translation trap; use keys, set locale explicitly in tests. (3) No pause, no tr(), no joypad bindings, no heal, no persistent enemy defeat, no menus: the game cannot yet be paused, localized, resumed per slot or finished. (4) Enemy attack clips never play and COMMIT is a dead AI state. (5) Docs are stale in places (AGENTS.md/ARCHITECTURE.md/new-enemy): CLAUDE.md + ecs-conversion-plan.md win. (6) The repo was committed to branch game-base while I worked; fresh worktrees need the generated-art build (README) or the lanes' tests will not load.

Dialogue choice: build the small Resource-based StoryBeat/StoryLine system now (AGENTS.md already says dialogue = typed .tres; zero dependency). If the owner wants a writer-friendly script format later, Dialogue Manager 4 (MIT, Godot 4.6+, headless/stateless, native translations) is the better addon; Dialogic 2 (Godot 4.5+, self-described Alpha, owns its own variables/saving/layout) is not advised. Both need owner approval.

RECOMMENDED SEQUENCE. Phase 0, one agent, serial, small commits: bus-layout fix + test; InputMap actions and pad bindings replacing raw KEY_ polling; GameEvents fan-out + data-driven system list + EcsWorld.frozen + EcsBoot options; WorldState schema v3 with slots/flags/meta (old signatures kept); i18n pipeline (locale/*.po, tr() wrappers, UI Theme); stale-doc and /verify refresh plus tests/run_all.sh. Phase 1, parallel lanes with disjoint file ownership (use separate branches/worktrees and the shared-hotspot list): A) Flow/UI: GameFlow, boot/title/pause/settings/slots/credits/world map. B) Story: StoryBeat/Box/BeatPlayer, TriggerMarker+TriggerSystem, prompts, placeholder beats and per-room wiring (one agent owns scenes/rooms/*). C) Combat/enemies: skills, child help, cell_effects, boss framework, rook/queen/king data, knockback/heal, JuiceDirector. D) World/audio/content: MusicManager, checkpoint/respawn, new zones and boss rooms, ending. Phase 2, integrator: end-to-end walk-through and ending tests, balance pass, export presets (currently gitignored and local-only), owner review handoffs. Owner decisions that block lanes: world model (#2, blocks map/zones), Knight/Bishop movement (#7), pickups reset on death (#6), child-whisper timing at T2 and the child's input key (#8), addon approval.

Emotion design is wired in as data hooks, not slogans: competence/autonomy/relatedness (https://selfdeterminationtheory.org/SDT/documents/2010_PrzybylskiRigbyRyan_ROGP.pdf) map to fair telegraphs, loops/shortcuts and the child's presence; death becomes narrative progress as in Hades (https://www.inlander.com/culture/hades-writer-greg-kasavin-on-how-he-made-video-game-deaths-drive-a-feel-good-story-22725237); the peak-end rule says spend polish on the boss climax and the ending (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peak%E2%80%93end_rule); hit-stop/shake/particles scale per event via an owner-tunable JuiceProfile; the opening stays quiet. These are design hypotheses to playtest with outsiders, not guarantees: docs/where-we-are.md records that no outside playtest has happened yet.
